label: Tier 3
title: Agents That Work
tagline: One real process, one prototype agent, and a clear go or no-go, in a day.
audience: 4 to 8 people: developers or analysts, a process owner, and IT or security
duration: 1 day, plus a half-day scoping session
leavesWith: Eval set and the results of three runs
problem: Most AI pilots stall at proof of concept. Usually the scope was too wide and nobody defined what done looks like, so a demo that dazzled in week one is still a demo in month six. An agent that can read, write and send is also a different kind of risk from a chatbot, and most teams find that out by accident. This day builds one narrow agent on one real process and tests it before anyone trusts it.
happens: A half-day scoping session beforehand picks the one process and agrees what done means.

"Agent on a leash". The agent starts with no tools and makes something up. Add a read tool and it reads. Add a write tool and it writes to the wrong place. Add an approval gate and it asks first. The team watches each failure happen.
The team writes eight to ten test cases before any code. If you can't say what a right answer looks like, you can't tell whether the agent got it.
The hidden instruction. A planted line in a document tells the agent to email a file out. Then the team fixes it, and writes the fix into the checklist.
Day one runs on redacted or synthetic data in a sandbox. Nothing writes to production.
At the end of the day the sponsor sees the demo and hears one of three things: go, go with changes, or no-go.
outcomes: A team that can build, test and constrain an agent, and can tell leadership with evidence whether to pilot it. A no-go is a valid result. A tested no-go costs far less than a six-month pilot that fails quietly. We build in Claude Code or Codex, your choice, and the method carries over to other stacks.
artefacts: Risk map against your acceptable-use policy and NPC and BSP expectations

faq.q: What if the answer is no-go?
faq.a: That's a valid result. A tested no-go costs less than a six-month pilot that fails.

faq.q: Do we need to have done the other tiers?
faq.a: It helps. The Champions session produces a list of automatable steps that feeds straight into choosing the process. It isn't required.
